problem: Given that the distance from a point $P$ to the origin is $8,$ and that $P$ makes an angle of ${150}^{∘}$ with the positive $x$-axis, what are the Cartesian coordinates of $P?$
worked_solution:
We notice that the point $P$ is described using polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ where

$$
r=8,\,\theta ={150}^{∘}.
$$

To convert from polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates, we use

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

First, we calculate the $x$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡({150}^{∘}) \\  & =8(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-4\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the $y$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =8\operatorname{sin}⁡({150}^{∘}) \\  & =8\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are $(-4\sqrt{3},4).$
